title: Best-First Width Search for Multi Agent Privacy-preserving Planning
review_status: full-text audit complete; privacy definition/leakage, search completeness, benchmark composition, single-goal coverage, distributed benchmarks, message exchange and five-run median protocol checked
sections_checked: Encrypted/dummy private-fact representations and stated leakage
CoDMAP/MBS distributed benchmarks, message metrics and five-run protocol
evidence_note: Across 3,404 single-goal instances, reported width-1/width-2 success rates are 77.59%/91.63%; hFF comparison is 96.94%. Domain results vary. Privacy encoding can let other agents infer the existence and truth value of a private fact and potentially private actions/causal effects; the paper calls for future study of fully protected models and privacy effects of pruning.

title: Signal Instructed Coordination in Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; policy-space theorem assumptions, shared state-independent signal, information regularization, matrix-game and predator-prey evaluations, ablations and random-seed counts checked
sections_checked: Limitations implicit in common signal/state-independent setup
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2019-09-10; published in Distributed Artificial Intelligence (DAI 2021), LNCS 13170, pp. 185–205, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-94662-3_12
evidence_note: A common per-episode signal expands decentralized policy expressivity under stated assumptions. Empirical tests include matrix games and 2v2/4v4 predator-prey; latter report 10 seeds. The signal is shared and state-independent during an episode; no lossy channel or deployment test was audited.

title: Learning Fairness in Multi-Agent Systems
review_status: full-text audit complete; fair-efficient reward, theorem assumptions, scenario definitions, fairness/efficiency metrics, baseline results, ablation and five-seed protocol checked
sections_checked: Five-seed protocol, hyperparameter caveat and conclusion
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2019-10-31; NeurIPS 2019, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32
evidence_note: FEN is evaluated in three constructed scenarios with five random seeds each. In job scheduling, FEN reports 90% utilization/CV 0.17 versus independent agents' 96%/1.57; in the other two testbeds it reports improvements in both scenario-specific fairness and efficiency outcomes. The paper notes sensitivity to α/β hyperparameters.
